items.title: 9.1.1 Design Thinking (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test)

source_refs.note: Topic 9.1.1 (PDF 208, printed 205). MCQ 2 is answered (b); the key gives (c). MCQ 4 (b) matches the key. Short question 2 is answered. Recorded.

blocks.title: Design thinking
blocks.text: Design thinking is a method for looking at problems from different angles: instead of jumping to solutions, you first understand the problem deeply. It has five steps: empathize, define, ideate, prototype and test.

items: Empathize: put yourself in users' shoes; talk to students about what they like and dislike about their school bags.
Define: state the problem clearly: students need a lightweight, durable, spacious bag that is comfortable to carry.
Ideate: brainstorm many ideas without worrying if they are perfect, such as extra padding or compartments.
Prototype: make a quick, simple version, such as a model from cardboard, fabric or paper.
Test: let students try it and give feedback, and improve it until it solves the problem.

blocks.alt: Left: five boxes in a cycle, Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype and Test, each with a school-bag example, and a red arrow from Test back to Empathize. Right: seven boxes for the parts of a business plan with short notes. Bottom: five pitch steps, problem, solution, unique point, audience and questions, using a juice shop.
blocks.caption: Design thinking, the business plan and the pitch (original diagram after topics 9.1 to 9.3).
blocks.long_description: Design thinking starts by empathizing with users, such as asking students about their bags, then defines the problem (a light, strong, roomy bag), ideates solutions (padding, pockets), builds a quick prototype (a cardboard model) and tests it with users; their feedback loops back to improve the design. A business plan covers the executive summary, business description, market analysis, organization and management, products or services, marketing and sales, and the financial plan. A pitch states the problem, the solution, what makes it unique and who it is for, and prepares for questions.

blocks.prompt: Which is a principle of design thinking (MCQ 2)? Which technique is common in it (MCQ 4)? What is its main focus (short question 2)?
blocks.explanation: (b) a human-centred approach; (b) brainstorming. Its main focus is the people who will use the product: understanding their needs deeply before designing, then testing with them and improving.

items: Design thinking: empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test, and repeat.
